title: BM25 Candidate-Pool Optimization Experiment
verdict_rationale: The heap top-k BM25 selection optimization is exactly equivalent to the full-sort baseline (235 real-query cases + 6/6 synthetic edge cases, max_rank_diff=0) and, combined with a BM25 candidate-pool cap of 250 and an experiment-local search_ranks primitive (avoids unnecessary BM25Result object construction), achieves end-to-end H3_RRF20 p95 = 693 ms and p99 = 748 ms — well under the proposed 2 s / 3 s gates — while preserving retrieval quality exactly (unit R@5 = 0.5385, source R@5 = 0.9783, evidence ceiling = 0.8372, ev0 = 7, matching the full-list control). All quality gates pass at pool >= 100; pool = 250 is the fastest eligible candidate with zero per-case regressions. Production defaults, frozen artifacts, and the existing application are unchanged.

baseline_profiling.bottleneck: BGE-M3 ENCODER (53% of total time). Within BM25: BM25Result object construction (12.6%) > scoring (9.2%) > sorting (5.7%).
baseline_profiling.key_finding: BM25 scores ~47k docs/query via postings and sorts ALL scored docs regardless of top_k. The candidate-pool cap does NOT reduce BM25 scoring or sorting work — only the BM25Result object building and dict/fusion input size.

candidate_pool_sweep.note: All variants use an experiment-local search_ranks primitive (returns rank/score dicts directly, no BM25Result objects). The pool cap applies ONLY to the BM25 input list to RRF; dense list is always full; RRF k=20, tie-breaking, evidence contract unchanged.

cost_attribution_answer.pool_cap_reduces_scoring_or_sorting: NO — BM25 still scores ~47k docs and sorts all scored docs regardless of pool size. The pool cap only reduces BM25Result object building and dict/fusion input size.
cost_attribution_answer.honest_finding: Per task section 2: truncating the BM25 list does NOT reduce the expensive scoring or sorting work. The fusion-input reduction is NOT a BM25 search optimization.

search_ranks.description: Experiment-local primitive that returns (rank_dict, score_dict) directly from the scored+sorted list, skipping BM25Result object construction for all ~47k scored docs. The hybrid path only needs rank/score dicts — the BM25Result objects are unnecessary work.
search_ranks.effect: Service-level baseline (builds 47k BM25Result objects): p50 847 ms, p95 2082 ms. With search_ranks (pool=full): p50 538 ms, p95 831 ms. ~60% p95 reduction from avoiding object construction alone.
search_ranks.exact_equivalence: Ranks and scores are identical to the original search(); only the wrapper objects are skipped.

heap_topk.description: heapq.nsmallest(top_k, scores.items(), key=(-score, doc_idx)) instead of full sorted()[:top_k]. O(m log k) vs O(m log m).
heap_topk.exact_equivalence: PASS — 235 real-query cases (5 pools x 47 queries) + 6/6 synthetic edge cases (equal scores tie-break, distinct scores, duplicate IDs, missing candidates, deterministic ranking, top_k > n_scored), max_rank_diff = 0.
heap_topk.note: Heap is only meaningful for bounded pools; full-list RRF still needs the full sort.

performance_gates.memory: peak RSS 3760 MB — no unacceptable increase (encoder dominates RSS)
performance_gates.cpu_contention: torch threads bounded to 2; existing app + Ollama preserved
performance_gates.reproducibility: 141 latency samples per variant (3 iters x 47 queries); deterministic CPU inference

recommendation.rationale: Fastest eligible candidate (p95 693 ms) with zero per-case regressions and all quality gates passing. pool=100 also passes but has 1 regression (002: rank 7->8) and higher p95 (767 ms). pool>=250 has 0 regressions; 250 is the fastest of these.
enabling_changes: search_ranks: avoid BM25Result object construction (experiment-local; the hybrid path only needs rank/score dicts)
heap top-k: heapq.nsmallest bounded selection instead of full sort (exact-equivalent; ~29% faster BM25 selection at pool=1000)
pool cap: limit BM25 candidate list supplied to RRF to 250 (dense list stays full; RRF k=20 unchanged)
recommendation.production_impact: NONE — all changes are experiment-local. Production retrieval remains H1 BM25 by default; H3_RRF20 is opt-in and its production implementation is unchanged.

limitations: The candidate-pool cap does NOT reduce BM25 scoring or sorting work (those still process all ~47k scored docs). The latency reduction comes primarily from avoiding BM25Result object construction (search_ranks), not from the pool cap itself.
The heap top-k optimization is only meaningful for bounded pools; full-list RRF still requires the full sort.
Encoder latency (53% of total) is unchanged by this experiment — it is the dominant cost and would require a faster encoder or GPU to reduce further.
Latency numbers vary with CPU contention (service-level baseline p95 ranged 1517-2407 ms across runs); the sweep numbers are from a single controlled run.
No generation evaluation was run (out of scope per task). Any material change to retrieved evidence would require a separate four-arm generation evaluation before rollout.
